payload.name: Reward-anticipation-driven motivation
payload.fact: Anticipated reward availability increases dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) activation, which then enhances pathways to the ventral tegmental area (VTA) and nucleus accumbens (NAcc) to initiate motivated behavior.
payload.boundary: Human fMRI study of reward anticipation.

provenance.title: Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex Drives Mesolimbic Dopaminergic Regions to Initiate Motivated Behavior
provenance.quote_or_locus: Specifically, our results indicated that dlPFC was the exclusive entry point of information about reward in this network, and that anticipated reward availability caused VTA activation only via its effect on the dlPFC. Anticipated reward thus increased dlPFC activation directly, whereas it influenced VTA and NAcc only indirectly, by enhancing intrinsically weak or inactive pathways from the dlPFC
